classification.habitat: Evergreen and semi-evergreen rain forests, often planted around temples and gardens.
classification.distribution: Eastern Himalaya from Nepal eastwards, Assam and North-East India, Bengal, Western Ghats (North Kanara, Konkan) and Andhra Pradesh.

identification.description: Golden-yellow stamens of Mesua ferrea flower; the dried stamens are the principal drug material.
identification.whole_plant: Evergreen tree, 15–18 m high, with a short often buttressed trunk and dense conical crown; young leaves red.
identification.stem: Straight trunk with dark ash-grey bark peeling in thin flakes.
identification.leaf: Simple, opposite, narrowly lanceolate, coriaceous, dark green above, glaucous white below; young flush crimson.
identification.flower: Large, fragrant, white four-petalled flowers with a central mass of numerous golden-yellow stamens.
identification.fruit: Ovoid, woody, pointed capsule with persistent sepals, 1–4 seeded.
identification.seed: Seeds large, angular, smooth and brown, yielding a fixed oil.
identification.bark: Ash-grey to reddish bark exfoliating in thin flakes, exuding a resin.
identification_points: Drug consists of dried stamens, coppery or golden brown
Each stamen 0.9–1.9 cm long with a linear basifixed anther
Filaments slender, twisted, united at base into a fleshy ring

therapeutics.precautions: Authenticate before use: the name Nagakeshara is also applied to flower buds of Ochrocarpus/Mammea and to Cinnamomum species in the market.
therapeutics.contraindications: Being Ushna and Ruksha, use with caution in dryness and constipation; avoid medicinal doses in pregnancy without supervision.

ज्वरकण्डूतृषास्वेदच्छर्दिहृल्लासनाशनम् ।
दौर्गन्ध्यकुष्ठवीसर्पकफपित्तविषापहम् ॥

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: API lists essential oil and oleo-resin in the stamens; coumarins and biflavonoids are reported from flowers and seeds.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Used primarily in bleeding disorders due to its astringent and hemostatic properties. It is also good for the skin.
recognized_uses: Traditional haemostatic in bleeding piles and menorrhagia
Ingredient of Nagakesaradi Churna and Kumaryasava
modern_information.safety_notes: Few safety data are available; substitution with other 'Nagakeshara' sources is common, so authentication is essential.
